data.narrative:
Radical AI is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $55M to date. The broader robotics and manufacturing sector includes one public comparable and eight private peers, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI. The company is led by Joseph F. Krause (CEO, formerly of Army Research Lab and AlleyCorp), Jorge Colindres (President, ex-AlleyCorp), and Prof. Gerbrand Ceder (CSO, UC Berkeley materials science, former MIT R.P. Simmons Professor).

Only one valuation method proved applicable to this analysis. The stage-progression approach, which applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression, yields an implied valuation of $138M when applied to the $55M raised proxy. A peer-median valuation could not be performed; while ten same-sector robotics and manufacturing peers exist, insufficient datapoints met narrower stage and valuation-tier filters (fewer than three comparable transactions), making sector-wide median analysis unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $117M (low) to $158M (high), with a median point of $138M. This range reflects uncertainty inherent in a single-method triangulation and the absence of direct comparable transactions at similar stage and scale. Key uncertainties include the applicability of standard seed-stage step-up multiples to frontier hardware, the company's path to revenue validation, and comparable exit multiples in robotics.
